title: How early should you arrive at Bournemouth Airport?
author: Matt
intro: Bournemouth is a small, one-terminal airport, and its own advice is to arrive at least two hours before your flight, even if you've checked in online. Here's how much time to allow, what to expect at security and how to get there.
seo_title: How early to get to Bournemouth Airport? 2 hours
seo_description: Bournemouth Airport says at least 2 hours before departure, even with online check-in. Check-in times, liquids, the 737 bus and the drop-off charge.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Airport's advice:** at least 2 hours
- **Check-in desks open:** 2 to 3 hours before
- **Early morning waves:** add 30 mins
- **Drop-off zone:** from £8, 30 mins

The airport's own guidance is to be at the terminal at least two hours before departure, even with online check-in. The deadlines that matter most are your airline's check-in and bag drop times, which are in your booking. Rules and charges change, so check with the airport or your airline before you fly. We checked the details below in November 2026.

sections.heading: Why two hours is about right
sections.text:
Bournemouth has one terminal and a short walk from check-in to security to the gates, so on a quiet day you'll be through quickly. But most flights are holiday flights, and they tend to leave in waves, with several Jet2, Ryanair and TUI departures close together early in the morning.

In those waves, the bag drop and security queues can build up fast, especially on summer Saturdays and in school holidays. Arriving two hours before gives you time for the queues and a coffee, without a long wait at the gate.

sections.heading: How early for your flight
sections.text:
| Flight | Our suggestion |
| --- | --- |
| Hand luggage only, checked in online | about 2 hours, as the airport advises |
| Holiday flight with hold bags | 2 hours, 2½ at busy times |
| First wave of the morning | 2½ hours |

Jet2 has a base at Bournemouth, and its winter 2026/27 programme includes the Canaries, a new route to [Málaga](/destinations/malaga), plus Portugal, Turkey, Mallorca and Morocco. Ryanair and TUI fly holiday routes too, with more in summer.

Tip: Jet2 and Ryanair close check-in and bag drop 40 minutes before departure, and other airlines are similar. Missing it means missing the flight, even if you're already in the terminal.

sections.heading: Security and liquids
sections.text:
Bournemouth has newer security scanners, and reports say you may no longer need to take liquids out of your bag. But reports differ on whether bigger containers are allowed, so the safe plan is to pack as if the standard rule still applies:

- **Liquids:** containers of 100ml or less, in a clear resealable bag.
- **Electronics:** be ready to take laptops and tablets out if asked.
- **Larger liquids:** pack them in your hold bag, or buy them after security.

Watch out: the airport you fly home from sets its own rules, and many still need liquids in a clear bag. Check Bournemouth's website before you pack, and keep a clear bag with you for the return flight.

sections.heading: After security
sections.text:
Once you're airside, there's one departure lounge with places to eat and drink and a duty-free shop, and the gates are close by. Small airports don't always call flights loudly, so keep an eye on the departure screens.

Boarding usually starts 30 to 40 minutes before departure, and the gate closes about 15 to 20 minutes before, so don't wait for a final call.

sections.heading: Getting to Bournemouth Airport
sections.text:
The airport is at Hurn, a few miles north of Bournemouth, close to Christchurch and Ferndown. There's no railway station at the airport.

- **By bus:** morebus route 737 links the airport with Bournemouth's rail and coach station in about 35 minutes, but it only runs a few times a day on weekdays, so check the timetable before you rely on it.
- **By car:** the drop-off zone has a barrier and charges from £8 for up to 30 minutes, paid on the way out. The airport's car parks are usually cheaper if you book ahead online.
- **By taxi:** around 20 minutes from Bournemouth town centre, depending on traffic. Taxis pay the same drop-off charge, which may be added to your fare.

For a dawn departure, the bus won't get you there in time, so most people drive, take a taxi or stay nearby the night before.

sections.heading: Where could you go from Bournemouth?
sections.text:
In winter, most of Bournemouth's flights head for the sun:

- **Warm winter sun:** [Tenerife](/destinations/tenerife) and [Lanzarote](/destinations/lanzarote), on UK time and about 21 to 22°C.
- **Shorter and milder:** [Málaga](/destinations/malaga), new with Jet2 this winter, and the [Algarve](/destinations/algarve).

Routes change every season, so check the airport's current destinations page before you plan. For more choice, [Southampton](/blog/how-early-should-you-arrive-at-southampton-airport) and [Bristol](/blog/where-can-you-fly-direct-from-bristol-airport) aren't far away. If you can't agree where to go, put your shortlist into a draw on somewhere.party.

faqs.question: How early should I get to Bournemouth Airport?
faqs.answer: The airport advises arriving at least two hours before departure, even if you've checked in online. Allow two and a half hours for early morning flights and school holidays.

faqs.question: When do check-in desks open at Bournemouth Airport?
faqs.answer: Usually two to three hours before the flight is due to leave. Jet2 and Ryanair close check-in and bag drop 40 minutes before departure.

faqs.question: How much is drop-off at Bournemouth Airport?
faqs.answer: When we checked, it was £8 for up to 30 minutes in the drop-off zone, paid at the barrier when you leave. Check the airport's website for current prices.

faqs.question: Is there a bus to Bournemouth Airport?
faqs.answer: Yes, morebus route 737 runs between Bournemouth rail and coach station and the airport in about 35 minutes, but only a few times a day on weekdays.
